title: Tet Hebrew Letter (ט): Sound & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Tet (ט): its [t] sound, its traditional link to טוֹב (good), words like בֶּטַח (sure), plus interactive practice.

editorialIssues.detail: The 'good' word-recognition distractor שלוֹם uses letters (Shin, Lamed, final Mem) not introduced in this lesson. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

blocks.0: Tet Hebrew Letter (ט): Sound, Words & Practice
blocks.5: The word טוֹב [tov] means 'good' and has one syllable. Tet (ט) gives [t]. Vav with Holam Male (וֹ) represents the vowel [o]; it does not add [v] in this word. Bet at the end of the word has no Dagesh (ב), so it gives [v]. Read the sounds together: [tov].
blocks.7: As a reply in conversation, בֶּטַח [be-tach] means 'sure' or 'of course.' In a sentence expressing an assumption, it can also mean 'probably.' The word has two syllables, with stress on the first: BE-tach. Bet with Dagesh (בּ) gives [b], and Segol beneath it adds [e]. Tet with Patah (טַ) gives [ta]. Chet at the end of the word (ח) adds [ch] to complete the second syllable [tach]. Here, ch represents the sound in German 'Bach' or Scottish 'loch'.
blocks.9: You have learned Tet (ט) and practised טוֹב [tov] and בֶּטַח [be-tach]. Remember that וֹ represents [o] in טוֹב; Bet at the end of the word, without Dagesh, provides [v]. If Segol or Patah still feels tricky, revisit the earlier lessons, then practise with the exercises below.

5.tip: The combination וֹ is called Holam Male and represents [o]. In טוֹב, this Vav is a vowel marker; Bet at the end of the word, without Dagesh, gives [v].

8.tip: Read בֶּטַח in two syllables: [be-tach], with stress on the first, BE-tach. The ch at the end represents the Chet sound; it adds no extra syllable.

10.tip: Tet (ט) is the 9th letter in the Hebrew alphabet.

theory.heading: Meet Tet
theory.intro: The ninth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Tet makes a plain [t] sound, as in “too,” and it begins the word for “good,” which you’ll hear in the greeting “boker tov.” In Modern Hebrew, Tet sounds exactly like Tav (ת), the last letter of the alphabet, so you have to learn which of the two each word is spelled with.
objectives: Read Tet in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">טוֹב</bdi> (good).

examples.heading: Tet in real words
examples.intro: See Tet in two new Hebrew words, and review the Holam Male, Segol and Patah vowel marks from earlier letters.
